claim: Tetrahymena thermophila maintains two functionally distinct nuclei within a common cytoplasm: a transcriptionally inert, heterochromatic micronucleus and a transcriptionally active, euchromatic macronucleus.
source: Tetrahymena maintain two functionally distinct nuclei within a common cytoplasm: a transcriptionally inert, heterochromatic micronucleus and a transcriptionally active, euchromatic macronucleus (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 1A showing co-immunofluorescence staining of Tetrahymena nuclei.

claim: The micronucleus contains the complete Tetrahymena genome whereas the genomic complexity of the macronucleus is reduced by approximately 33% through programmed DNA elimination.
source: The micronucleus contains the complete Tetrahymena genome whereas the genomic complexity of the macronucleus (derived from the micronucleus during sexual reproduction) is reduced by ∼33% through programmed DNA elimination (http://www.broadinstitute.org/annotation/genome/Tetrahymena/MultiHome.html).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with reference to the Tetrahymena genome database.

claim: Most of the eliminated, micronuclear-limited sequences are repetitive, centromeric, or otherwise non-coding DNA.
source: Most of the eliminated, micronuclear-limited sequences are repetitive, centromeric, or otherwise non-coding DNA (Chalker, 2008; Schoeberl et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by citations to Chalker, 2008 and Schoeberl et al., 2012.

claim: Micronuclear histone H3 occurs in two electrophoretically distinct forms in vivo: H3S (slow form) and H3F (fast form).
source: As expected, micronuclear H3 occurs in two electrophoretically distinct forms in vivo (Figure 1C, inset): the slow form of micronuclear H3 (H3S) is the same sequence as macronuclear H3; and the fast form (H3F) is derived from H3S during a micronucleus-specific proteolytic processing step that removes the first six amino acids from the H3S N-terminus (Allis et al., 1980).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 1C showing the two H3 species, with citation to Allis et al., 1980.

claim: H3F is derived from H3S during a micronucleus-specific proteolytic processing step that removes the first six amino acids from the H3S N-terminus.
source: the fast form (H3F) is derived from H3S during a micronucleus-specific proteolytic processing step that removes the first six amino acids from the H3S N-terminus (Allis et al., 1980).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by citation to Allis et al., 1980.

claim: Micronuclear H3S and H3F are collectively hypoacetylated, deficient in H3K4me, and enriched for H3K27me.
source: Our HILIC-MS/MS analysis revealed that, similar to condensed chromatin in higher eukaryotes (Jeppesen and Turner, 1993), micronuclear H3S and H3F were collectively hypoacetylated, deficient in H3K4me, and enriched for H3K27me (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 1D showing mass spectrometry data, with citation to Jeppesen and Turner, 1993.

claim: H3K9me was not detected on any species of vegetative micronuclear H3.
source: As expected from our previous studies, H3K9me was not detected on any species of vegetative micronuclear H3, while H3K27me3 and the mitotic PTM, histone H3 serine 10 phosphorylation (H3S10ph), were only detected on H3F (Wei et al., 1998; Taverna et al., 2007b).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by citations to Wei et al., 1998 and Taverna et al., 2007b.

claim: H3K27me3 and H3S10ph were only detected on H3F in vegetative micronuclear H3.
source: As expected from our previous studies, H3K9me was not detected on any species of vegetative micronuclear H3, while H3K27me3 and the mitotic PTM, histone H3 serine 10 phosphorylation (H3S10ph), were only detected on H3F (Wei et al., 1998; Taverna et al., 2007b).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by citations to Wei et al., 1998 and Taverna et al., 2007b.

claim: Methylation on H3K23 was detected in Tetrahymena micronuclei, which was highly enriched on H3F and mostly occurred in combination with H3K27me.
source: Unexpectedly, we detected methylation on H3K23, which was highly enriched on H3F and mostly occurred in combination with H3K27me (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 1D showing mass spectrometry data.

claim: H3K23me3/H3K27me3 PTM state was most abundant out of all the dually methylated H3K23/H3K27 states.
source: We focused on H3K23me3 since it was highly associated with H3K27me3 and the H3K23me3/H3K27me3 PTM state was most abundant out of all the dually methylated H3K23/H3K27 states (Figure 1D, red asterisks).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 1D showing mass spectrometry data.

claim: The α-H3K23me3 antibody is highly specific for peptides containing the H3K23me3 mark.
source: As shown in Figure 2B, the antibody was highly specific for peptides containing the H3K23me3 mark.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2B showing ELISA analysis.

claim: Preincubation of the α-H3K23me3 antibody with excess H3K23me3 peptide, but not H3K4me3, H3K9me3, or H3K27me3 peptides, competed away immunoreactivity for H3K23me3.
source: Furthermore, preincubation of the antibody with excess H3K23me3 peptide, but not H3K4me3, H3K9me3, or H3K27me3 peptides, competed away immunoreactivity for H3K23me3 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2C showing ELISA analysis.

claim: The α-H3K23me3 antibody did not bind to the H3K9me3 peptide, even though the neighboring sequence of H3K9 is very similar to that of H3K23.
source: Notably, α-H3K23me3 antibodies did not bind to the H3K9me3 peptide, even though the neighboring sequence of H3K9 is very similar to that of H3K23 (Figure 2A, yellow boxes).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2A showing sequence alignment.

claim: The presence of H3K27me3 did not occlude the α-H3K23me3 antibody from binding to the dual H3K23me3/H3K27me3 PTM state.
source: Thus, the antibody is highly specific for H3K23me3, and importantly, the presence of H3K27me3 did not occlude it from binding to the dual H3K23me3/H3K27me3 PTM state we identified in Tetrahymena.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text based on the antibody characterization data.

claim: H3K23me3 was only present on the proteolytically processed H3F from micronuclei, but not H3S from micronuclei or macronuclei.
source: The results showed that H3K23me3 was only present on the proteolytically processed H3F from micronuclei, but not H3S from micronuclei or macronuclei (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2D showing Western blot analysis.

claim: H3K23me3 was exclusively localized to germline micronuclei in Tetrahymena.
source: Indirect immunofluorescence using α-H3K23me3 further confirmed that H3K23me3 was exclusively localized to germline micronuclei in Tetrahymena (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 2E showing immunofluorescence staining.

claim: H3K23me3 is not detectable on macronuclear H3.
source: Coupled with the fact that H3K23me3 is not detectable on macronuclear H3 (Taverna et al., 2007b), our results indicate that this PTM is exclusive to the Tetrahymena germline.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by citation to Taverna et al., 2007b.

claim: H3K23me3 is exclusive to the Tetrahymena germline.
source: Coupled with the fact that H3K23me3 is not detectable on macronuclear H3 (Taverna et al., 2007b), our results indicate that this PTM is exclusive to the Tetrahymena germline.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text based on the data presented and citation to Taverna et al., 2007b.

claim: H3K23me3 levels greatly increase on H3F during conjugation, peaking by hour approximately 4, and diminishing to levels observed in vegetative cells by hour 8.
source: Whole-cell-extracts collected at key time points during conjugation revealed that H3K23me3 levels greatly increase on H3F, peaking by hour ∼4, and diminishing to levels observed in vegetative cells by hour 8 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 3A showing Western blot analysis.

claim: Up-regulation of H3K23me3 early in conjugation implied a connection to meiosis.
source: Interestingly, up-regulation of H3K23me3 early in conjugation implied a connection to meiosis, which precedes mitosis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as an inference from the timing of H3K23me3 upregulation.

claim: H3K23me3 levels increase before the mitosis-associated PTM H3S10ph becomes enriched.
source: Indeed, H3K23me3 levels increase before the mitosis-associated PTM H3S10ph becomes enriched (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 3B showing Western blot analysis.

claim: Increased H3K23me3 coincided with meiotic entry.
source: While increased H3K23me3 coincided with meiotic entry, the PTM was still present, although much reduced, during stages of mitosis as evidenced by our Western blot (Figure 3B), immunofluorescence (Figure 3C), and HILIC-MS/MS data (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by multiple figures showing Western blot, immunofluorescence, and mass spectrometry data.

claim: H3K23me3 was still present, although much reduced, during stages of mitosis.
source: While increased H3K23me3 coincided with meiotic entry, the PTM was still present, although much reduced, during stages of mitosis as evidenced by our Western blot (Figure 3B), immunofluorescence (Figure 3C), and HILIC-MS/MS data (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by multiple figures showing Western blot, immunofluorescence, and mass spectrometry data.

claim: H3FK27me3 levels in the micronucleus increased and diminished concurrently with H3K23me3 levels during conjugation.
source: While H3SK27me3 levels in the macronucleus remain constant throughout conjugation (Liu et al., 2007), we found that H3FK27me3 levels in the micronucleus increased and diminished concurrently with H3K23me3 levels (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 3B showing Western blot analysis, with citation to Liu et al., 2007.

claim: Up-regulated H3K23me3 remained physically linked to H3K27me3 in micronuclear histone H3 purified from conjugating cells.
source: Our HILIC-MS/MS analysis of micronuclear histone H3 purified from conjugating cells also showed that up-regulated H3K23me3 remained physically linked to H3K27me3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1A showing mass spectrometry data.

claim: H3K9me3 was only detected after levels of H3K23me3 diminished during conjugation.
source: In contrast to the coordinate increase of H3K23me3 and H3K27me3 observed during meiosis, H3K9me3, which specifically emerges during nuclear differentiation (Liu et al., 2007; Taverna et al., 2002), was only detected after levels of H3K23me3 diminished (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 3B showing Western blot analysis, with citations to Liu et al., 2007 and Taverna et al., 2002.

claim: Low levels of H3K23me3 detected during nuclear differentiation are present in micronuclei and not the H3K9me3-enriched developing macronuclei.
source: The fact that low levels of H3K23me3 detected during nuclear differentiation are present in micronuclei and not the H3K9me3-enriched developing macronuclei (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), further defines distinct functions within heterochromatin for these PTMs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1B showing immunofluorescence staining.

claim: H3K23me3 may play an important new role during meiosis and heterochromatin formation.
source: Taken together, these findings suggest that H3K23me3 may play an important new role during meiosis and heterochromatin formation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a conclusion from the data presented.

claim: H3K23me3 was present at wild type levels in ΔEZL1 cells.
source: While H3K23me3 was present at wild type levels in ΔEZL1 cells, their levels were significantly reduced in ΔEZL2 cells and completely undetectable in ΔEZL3 cells (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 4A-B showing Western blot and immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: H3K23me3 levels were significantly reduced in ΔEZL2 cells.
source: While H3K23me3 was present at wild type levels in ΔEZL1 cells, their levels were significantly reduced in ΔEZL2 cells and completely undetectable in ΔEZL3 cells (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 4A-B showing Western blot and immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: H3K23me3 was completely undetectable in ΔEZL3 cells.
source: While H3K23me3 was present at wild type levels in ΔEZL1 cells, their levels were significantly reduced in ΔEZL2 cells and completely undetectable in ΔEZL3 cells (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 4A-B showing Western blot and immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: Ezl3p expression was required for H3K23me1 and H3K23me2 in addition to H3K23me3.
source: In addition to H3K23me3, Ezl3p expression was required for H3K23me1 and H3K23me2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C showing Western blot analysis.

claim: Mass spectrometric analysis of all micronuclear core histones from ΔEZL3 cells revealed that only H3K23 methylation is lost in these mutants.
source: In line with these results, mass spectrometric analysis of all micronuclear core histones from ΔEZL3 cells revealed that only H3K23 methylation is lost in these mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1,F).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1F showing mass spectrometry data.

claim: H3K23 is the likely target for Ezl3p activity in micronuclei.
source: Together, these results implicate H3K23 as the likely target for Ezl3p activity in micronuclei.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a conclusion from the data presented.

claim: Ezl3 expression was strongly upregulated during early conjugation.
source: Ezl3 expression was strongly upregulated during early conjugation, further supporting an integral role for Ezl3 in meiosis and H3K23 methylation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1D showing qPCR data.

claim: Expression of wild type Ezl3p, but not Ezl3pH599A, rescued the levels of H3K23me3 in ΔEZL3 cells.
source: As shown in Figure 4C, expression of wild type Ezl3p, but not Ezl3pH599A, rescued the levels of H3K23me3 in ΔEZL3 cells.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 4C showing Western blot analysis.

claim: Catalytically active Ezl3p is necessary and sufficient for the deposition of H3K23me3 in Tetrahymena in vivo.
source: While these results demonstrate catalytically active Ezl3p is necessary and sufficient for the deposition of H3K23me3 in Tetrahymena in vivo, we were not able to purify Ezl3 in amounts sufficient to examine Ezl3 methylation of H3K23 in vitro.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a conclusion from the rescue experiment data.

claim: In log phase, the growth rate of ΔEZL3 cells was about 20% slower than wild type cells.
source: In log phase, the growth rate of ΔEZL3 cells was about 20% slower than wild type cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1 showing growth curve data.

claim: A significant lag was detected during early conjugation in ΔEZL3 cells, exemplified by a delay in the onset of H3S10ph.
source: Remarkably, a significant lag was detected during early conjugation in ΔEZL3 cells, exemplified by a delay in the onset of H3S10ph.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text based on Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The developmental delay of ΔEZL3 cells became more pronounced during nuclear differentiation, as highlighted by levels of Pdd1p at later stages of conjugation.
source: Moreover, the developmental delay of ΔEZL3 cells became more pronounced during nuclear differentiation, as highlighted by levels of Pdd1p at later stages of conjugation (Figures 5A, 18hr–48hr).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 5A showing Western blot analysis.

claim: The initial lag during conjugation in ΔEZL3 cells began at the leptotene/zygotene stages of meiotic prophase.
source: Cytologic comparison of wild type and ΔEZL3 mating pairs showed that the initial lag during conjugation began at the leptotene/zygotene stages of meiotic prophase (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 5B showing cytological analysis.

claim: ΔEZL3 cells showed delayed formation of piRNA-like scanRNA.
source: ΔEZL3 cells also showed delayed formation of piRNA-like scanRNA (Figure 5C), a class of non-coding RNAs intricately involved with heterochromatin formation and DNA elimination at the nuclear differentiation stage of conjugation (Mochizuki et al., 2002; Liu et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 5C showing RNA gel analysis, with citations to Mochizuki et al., 2002 and Liu et al., 2007.

claim: Despite a pronounced lag in the completion of meiosis, nuclear differentiation, and scanRNA formation, ΔEZL3 cells eventually proceeded to terminal stages of conjugation.
source: Despite a pronounced lag in the completion of meiosis, nuclear differentiation, and scanRNA formation, ΔEZL3 cells eventually proceeded to terminal stages of conjugation (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 5B showing cytological analysis.

claim: During meiosis, the programmed formation of DNA double-strand breaks (DSB) facilitates loci pairing and homolog segregation and promotes recombination and genetic diversity.
source: During meiosis, the programmed formation of DNA double-strand breaks (DSB) facilitates loci pairing and homolog segregation and promotes recombination and genetic diversity (Lichten and de Massy, 2011).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by citation to Lichten and de Massy, 2011.

claim: Misregulation of DSB pathways within the germline can reduce genomic stability, the production of viable gametes, and progeny viability.
source: Misregulation of DSB pathways within the germline can reduce genomic stability, the production of viable gametes, and progeny viability (Brachet et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by citation to Brachet et al., 2012.

claim: Phosphorylation on the C-terminus of histone H2A.X (γH2A.X) is a well-known indicator of the presence of DSBs and the ensuing DNA damage response in a myriad of organisms including Tetrahymena.
source: Conveniently, phosphorylation on the C-terminus of histone H2A.X (γH2A.X) is a well-known indicator of the presence of DSBs and the ensuing DNA damage response, in a myriad of organisms including Tetrahymena, and α-γH2A.X is also used to assess meiotic progression (Song et al., 2007 and references therein).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by citation to Song et al., 2007.

claim: Micronuclear chromosomes in early stages of meiosis become highly organized with centromeres and highly-repetitive pericentric regions (DAPI-poor) segregating to one pole of the elongating micronucleus, while telomeres and genic regions (DAPI-rich) localize to the opposite pole.
source: Micronuclear chromosomes in early stages of meiosis become highly organized—centromeres and highly-repetitive pericentric regions (DAPI-poor) segregate to one pole of the elongating micronucleus, while telomeres and genic regions (DAPI-rich) localize to the opposite pole (Figure 6A) (Loidl and Scherthan, 2004; Mochizuki et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 6A showing immunofluorescence images, with citations to Loidl and Scherthan, 2004 and Mochizuki et al., 2008.

claim: DSBs in wild type micronuclei initiated early in meiosis (leptotene/zygotene) within the DAPI-rich genic region, becoming distributed throughout the micronucleus by pachytene.
source: As illustrated in Figure 6A, DSBs in wild type micronuclei initiated early in meiosis (leptotene/zygotene) within the DAPI-rich genic region, becoming distributed throughout the micronucleus by pachytene.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 6A showing immunofluorescence images.

claim: In early meiotic ΔEZL3 micronuclei, while some DSB signal could be detected in the DAPI-rich genic region, the vast majority of DSB signal covered the DAPI-poor, centromeric pole of micronuclei.
source: In striking contrast, while some DSB signal in early meiotic ΔEZL3 micronuclei could be detected in the DAPI-rich genic region, the vast majority of DSB signal covered the DAPI-poor, centromeric pole of micronuclei (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 6A showing immunofluorescence images.

claim: In meiotic ΔEZL3 cells, the increased DSB signal over the DAPI-poor, centromeric pole of micronuclei remained for the majority of the meiotic lag, although when mutant cells finally entered pachytene, γH2A.X localization resembled wild type distribution.
source: In meiotic ΔEZL3 cells, the increased DSB signal over the DAPI-poor, centromeric pole of micronuclei remained for the majority of the meiotic lag, although when mutant cells finally entered pachytene, γH2A.X localization resembled wild type distribution (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 6A showing immunofluorescence images.

claim: DSBs were not mislocalized in ΔEZL2 cells (lacking H3K27me3).
source: Interestingly, DSBs were not mislocalized in ΔEZL2 cells (lacking H3K27me3), suggesting that only cells completely lacking H3K23me3 have mislocalized meiotic DSBs (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 6B showing immunofluorescence images.

claim: Only cells completely lacking H3K23me3 have mislocalized meiotic DSBs.
source: Interestingly, DSBs were not mislocalized in ΔEZL2 cells (lacking H3K27me3), suggesting that only cells completely lacking H3K23me3 have mislocalized meiotic DSBs (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 6B showing immunofluorescence images.

claim: Centromeric H3 (α-Cna1p) was similarly positioned in both wild type and ΔEZL3 cells, showing that the shift in DSB positioning in ΔEZL3 cells was not the result of massive chromatin reorganization within the nuclei.
source: Centromeric H3 (α-Cna1p) was similarly positioned in both wild type and ΔEZL3 cells, showing that the shift in DSB positioning in ΔEZL3 cells was not the result of massive chromatin reorganization within the nuclei (Figure 6C) (Cervantes et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 6C showing immunofluorescence images, with citation to Cervantes et al., 2006.

claim: A number of micronuclear-limited sequences, including Tlr1, are repetitive in nature and are enriched in centromere-proximal regions, whereas genes are enriched more distally on the chromosome arms.
source: A number of micronuclear-limited sequences, including Tlr1, are repetitive in nature and are enriched in centromere-proximal regions, whereas genes are enriched more distally on the chromosome arms (EP Hamilton and RS Coyne, personal communication).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by personal communication.

claim: In wild type meiotic micronuclei, minimal overlap was detected between the α-γH2A.X and Tlr1 probe signals.
source: In wild type meiotic micronuclei, we detected minimal overlap between the α-γH2A.X and Tlr1 probe signals.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text based on immunoFISH data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: In ΔEZL3 cells, α-γH2A.X and Tlr1 probe signals were highly overlapping and enriched near the centromeric pole of meiotic micronuclei.
source: However in ΔEZL3 cells, these signals were highly overlapping and enriched near the centromeric pole of meiotic micronuclei, further suggesting that DSBs in cells lacking H3K23me3 are mislocalized to pericentric regions (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 6D showing immunoFISH images.

claim: DSBs in cells lacking H3K23me3 are mislocalized to pericentric regions.
source: However in ΔEZL3 cells, these signals were highly overlapping and enriched near the centromeric pole of meiotic micronuclei, further suggesting that DSBs in cells lacking H3K23me3 are mislocalized to pericentric regions (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 6D showing immunoFISH images.

claim: Although parental ΔEZL3 cells reach terminal cytological stages of conjugation, the progeny viability was significantly impaired.
source: Although parental ΔEZL3 cells reach terminal cytological stages of conjugation (Figure 5B, 48 hr), the progeny viability was significantly impaired (Figure 6E and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 6E showing progeny viability data.

claim: Fertility was negatively affected when surviving ΔEZL3 progeny were backcrossed to wild type cells.
source: Furthermore, fertility was also negatively affected when surviving ΔEZL3 progeny were backcrossed to wild type cells (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text based on unpublished data.

claim: H3K23me3 helps mediate the formation of a higher-order chromatin structure during meiosis that is distinct from H3K9me3-associated heterochromatin.
source: Taken together, we hypothesize that H3K23me3 helps mediate the formation of a higher-order chromatin structure during meiosis that is distinct from H3K9me3-associated heterochromatin.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a hypothesis based on the data presented.

claim: H3K23me3-enriched heterochromatin helps to protect pericentric, repetitive genetic sequences from meiotic DSBs, which are catalyzed by the opportunistic and highly conserved Spo11 nuclease.
source: Our observations further suggest that H3K23me3-enriched heterochromatin helps to protect pericentric, repetitive genetic sequences from meiotic DSBs, which are catalyzed by the opportunistic and highly conserved Spo11 nuclease (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a suggestion based on the data presented, with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2 showing a model.

claim: H3K23me3 was present in C. elegans chromatin, although at a much lower abundance than in Tetrahymena micronuclear chromatin.
source: Comparative Western blot analysis of whole-embryo nuclear extracts showed that H3K23me3 was present in C. elegans chromatin, although at a much lower abundance than in Tetrahymena micronuclear chromatin (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 7A showing Western blot analysis.

claim: H3K23me3 was nearly absent in the mitotic region of the C. elegans gonad, although a small number of mitotic nuclei in this region were positive for the PTM.
source: By indirect immunofluorescence, H3K23me3 was nearly absent in the mitotic region of the gonad, although a small number of mitotic nuclei in this region were positive for the PTM (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 7C showing immunofluorescence staining.

claim: H3K23me3 staining became robust in meiotic cells within the C. elegans gonad, beginning at the leptotene/zygotene transition zone that marks meiotic entry, and plateauing through the rest of meiotic prophase.
source: In striking contrast, H3K23me3 staining became robust in meiotic cells within the gonad, beginning at the leptotene/zygotene transition zone that marks meiotic entry, and plateauing through the rest of meiotic prophase (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A showing immunofluorescence staining.

claim: Compared to H3K27me3, H3K9me3, and H3K4me3 distribution in the C. elegans gonad, H3K23me3 was the only PTM that became enriched as germ cells entered the transition zone.
source: Compared to H3K27me3, H3K9me3, and H3K4me3 distribution in the gonad, H3K23me3 was the only PTM that became enriched as germ cells entered the transition zone (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B showing immunofluorescence staining.

claim: H3K23me3 appeared relatively punctate across the entire nucleus in C. elegans meiotic cells rather than being enriched on either the autosomes or the silenced Xs.
source: Notably, H3K23me3 appeared relatively punctate across the entire nucleus rather than being enriched on either the autosomes (such as H3K4me3) or the silenced Xs (such as H3K27me3) (Kelly et al., 2002; Bender et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7E, with citations to Kelly et al., 2002 and Bender et al., 2004.

claim: In the gonad of mes-2 knockout strains, H3K27me3 was completely undetectable.
source: As expected, in the gonad of mes-2 knockout strains, H3K27me3 was completely undetectable (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 7—figure supplement 1E showing immunofluorescence staining.

claim: In mes-2 knockout strains, H3K23me3 remained present in meiotic cells, and H3K23me3 levels within the mitotic germ cell region increased.
source: In contrast, H3K23me3 remained present in meiotic cells, and surprisingly, H3K23me3 levels within the mitotic germ cell region increased (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 7—figure supplement 1E showing immunofluorescence staining.

claim: H3K23me3 remained detectable in mitotic and meiotic regions of the mes-4(RNAi) germline.
source: Similar to mes-2 knockouts, H3K23me3 remained detectable in mitotic and meiotic regions of the mes-4(RNAi) germline (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 7—figure supplement 1F showing immunofluorescence staining.

claim: Neither MES-2 nor MES-4 is exclusively responsible for trimethylation of H3K23 in C. elegans.
source: Nevertheless, our data suggest neither MES-2 nor MES-4 is exclusively responsible for trimethylation of H3K23 in C. elegans.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a conclusion from the data presented.

claim: In the GLP-1 loss-of-function mutant glp-1(lf), which undergoes early differentiation of mitotic cells and early entry into meiosis, a shift of the H3K23me3 signal towards the distal tip of the gonad was observed.
